messages:
sara_support: Customer OrbitPay (prod) opened a P1 — sudden drop in response quality after an automated failover to EU. They report short/garbled replies and occasional 500s. Ticket #12345. cc @liam_oncall
ops_bot: routing-engine: auto-failover triggered for route=orbitpay-prod, reason=capacity_pressure, target_pool=eu-west-2-backup, served_model=rw-v2-small-quant-q4_1
tessa_prod: oh no — OrbitPay config pins model=rw-v2-large. They should not be served rw-v2-small. :grimacing:
sara_support: reproducible example from the customer (sanitized):

Request:
POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>, X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-2
Body: {"model":"rw-v2-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize invoice #A-119 in one sentence"}], "max_tokens":64}

Response (unexpected): HTTP 200
{"id":"...","model":"rw-v2-small-quant-q4_1","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Invoice A-119 paid. ref 0xF2\u0000\u0000"}}]}

And sometimes a 500 with a short error: `decode_error: tokenizer mismatch: unexpected byte 0xfc`

liam_oncall: can you paste the exact timestamps and a sample request_id? need logs from router and runtime. also did they hit any 401/403s?
sara_support: sample request_id=rq_0b9c4e. timestamps: first alert 2026-02-12T08:03:19Z. There were 3x 401s earlier in the morning due to a rotated webhook secret (separate ticket), but the quality drop correlates with the failover window 08:03-08:21 UTC.
ash_infra: looking at routing rules for orbitpay-prod: `route { match: customer_id:orbitpay; preferred_region: eu-west-2; failover_policy: { mode: best_effort, compatible_variants: [] } }` — best_effort allows any variant when capacity is low. I see backup pool advertised model `rw-v2-small-quant-q4_1` (quantized) which uses `rw-tokenizer-v1` rather than `rw-tokenizer-v2`.

mark_research: that tokenizer mismatch is the smoking gun. rw-v2-large expects rw-tokenizer-v2 vocab mapping. When we fall back to rw-v2-small-quant, we use a different vocabulary and byte->token mapping. That explains garbled outputs and different token counts (customer reported doubled token billing in logs).

mike_platform: billing noticed tokenization churn in the same window: backend token_count spikes ~2x for some requests (re-tokenization + fallback). Not a charge bug, but explains surprising usage. We should avoid cross-tokenizer fallbacks for pinned models.

liam_oncall: immediate remediation options: 1) rollback routing so orbitpay-prod points to eu-primary only (undo failover) 2) set failover_policy.mode=strict for pinned customers 3) add an on-the-fly tokenizer shim that translates tokens (risky). Which do we prefer for short term?

tessa_prod: we rolled back to rw-v2-large in eu-west-2-backup at 08:40 UTC and customer confirmed responses look normal again. They accepted rollback. Need patch so this doesn't recur.

mark_research: longer term: routing should include tokenizer_id in compatibility checks. compatible_variants should only include variants that share tokenizer_id and comparable decoding behavior. We also should add a check that quantized variants expose `tokenizer_alias` metadata.

ash_infra: quick config snippet to avoid recurrence:
```
route {
  match: customer_id:orbitpay
  failover_policy: {
    mode: strict
    require: ["tokenizer_id:rw-tokenizer-v2", "min_capabilities:text-generation"]
  }
}
```

sara_support: customer impact summary I sent: quality regression + transient billing spikes + a couple of 500s. Customer was upset but understands rollback. They asked for a postmortem and ETA for a permanent fix.

mike_platform: action items: 1) patch routing service to check tokenizer_id metadata (liam/ash). 2) add telemetry alert for any route where served_model.tokenizer != requested_model.tokenizer (mark). 3) billing to reconcile the doubled token counts and attach to the ticket (mike).

liam_oncall: assigning eng-runtime @mark_research and infra @ash_infra to create a hotfix. I opened ENG-3247. Tentative ETA for hotfix: 48 hours. I'll own the rollback if it flaps.

ops_bot: incident-note: created incident INC-20260212-01, severity=high, status=triaged, owner=@liam_oncall

tessa_prod: customer notified about rollback and the incident. They'll hold on immediate SLA credits for now pending postmortem. :thumbsup:

mark_research: suggestion for tests: add integration test in routing that spins up a backup pool with different tokenizer and verifies failovers are rejected when `failover_policy.mode=strict` for pinned configs. Also add unit test to validate tokenizer metadata propagation.

liam_oncall: moving to follow-up channel for postmortem. closing thread here.
